topic: Balancing Redox Reactions: Oxidation Number Method
title: Oxidation Number Method Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A see-saw stays level only when both sides weigh the same. In this animated lesson for Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 7, Redox Reactions) Diya weighs rice on a kitchen pan scale, and we learn how chemists weigh electrons to balance a redox reaction.

You will see why electrons lost must equal electrons gained, then balance dichromate and sulphite in acid on the molecule bench: chromium falls from +6 to +3 (two Cr atoms gain 6 electrons), sulphur rises from +4 to +6 (each sulphite loses 2), so we take three sulphites. We finish in five steps: oxidation numbers, rise = fall, fix the charge with H+, balance hydrogen with water, check oxygen. Then we compare acid and basic solutions (H+ or OH-), balance permanganate and bromide in a basic solution, show the per-atom trap, solve an original JEE Main pattern question, and end with a recap card and three questions to check yourself. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.

This is Episode 74 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students.

In this video:

2:05 Acid vs base, pause and think
